item.title: China’s Belt and Road must adapt to survive a hotter world
item.description: Development projects globally must answer a burning question as rising temperatures threaten workers’ health and productivity, write three academics.

item.title: Singapore bank faces complaint to SGX over Indonesian coal-powered nickel financing
item.description: NGO argues that OCBC disclosures do not fully reflect the climate risks from captive coal plants, breaching SGX rules on sustainability reporting. OCBC says its disclosures do not break SGX rules.

item.title: Could Chinese miners be facing stronger environmental standards?
item.description: A series of new guidelines aim to standardise and mainstream ESG reporting by Chinese mining companies, but gaps remain.

item.title: Q&A: ‘India must ready tools to prevent virus outbreaks’
item.description: Infant deaths in India have declined, but viral infection rates remain high, underscoring that water and sanitation alone cannot prevent viral disease and that vaccine gains must be reinforced by pandemic preparedness.

item.title: India's pesticide reforms overlooks human health
item.description: India’s pesticide industry has grown into a multi-billion-rupee sector, even as concerns over health, environmental and food safety have intensified.

item.title: WASTED the documentary now streaming on Eco-Business
item.description: Eco-Business subscribers can now stream the acclaimed impact documentary WASTED (2025), as the platform expands its video content offering for its community.

item.title: South Korea’s ESG finance hits record $1.5 trillion but momentum fades
item.description: High borrowing costs and weak policy signals slow growth, while social lending dominates over climate funding, a new report finds.

item.title: Trump’s EPA decides climate change doesn’t endanger public health – the evidence says otherwise
item.description: The Trump administration’s arguments in dismissing the health risks of climate change are not only factually wrong, they’re deeply dangerous to public health and safety.

item.title: Warming winters are disrupting the hidden world of fungi – the result can shift mountain grasslands to scrub
item.description: Warmer winters are affecting the nutrient cycles that plants rely on to survive.

item.title: Every click has a cost: Singapore’s push to make digital use more sustainable
item.description: As AI and cloud use surge, the city-state explores new ways to cut the rising energy footprint of digital services.
